$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE (REC-vc-jose-cose-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own. Source .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.bin, sha256 6c70cf8d7de9d8a3ff28a743fea9d569a67a402111c3245fdafbaa2ad6709af9; quotations of the source are checked against its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.txt, sha256 f02bd4966800863d533746c6c39ad267ada1b8bfcbb92186c204b617bb46c126. Quotations of other documents are checked against the copies README.md lists with their digests. INSTANCE: the unsecured credential or presentation, a JSON object: the decoded JWS payload of application/vc+jwt or application/vp+jwt, the JWT Claims Set an SD-JWT verifier rebuilds from the Issuer-signed payload and the disclosures (§5.2), or the COSE_Sign1 payload of application/vc+cose or application/vp+cose decoded as JSON. The raw Issuer-signed SD-JWT payload, with its digests, is sd-jwt.derived.schema.json's. LEVELS. The root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules: a failure is non-conformance. A rule marked imported is a MUST of another document, named with the clause of this source that makes it bind. Anchors ending in -should add the SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED and NOT RECOMMENDED statements and include the MUST level by reference: a failure there is a deviation from a recommendation, to be reported as a warning, never as non-conformance. A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. The root holds for every securing mechanism; #jwt adds what holds for a JWT Claims Set (JWS and SD-JWT). There is no -should level here: the RECOMMENDED proof-of-possession binding may sit in a header or in the claims, so it is cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-07. §3.1.3, which carries the JOSE advice on iat, exp and nbf, is marked non-normative and contributes no constraint.
title: Secured payload: the credential or presentation, and its JWT Claims Set (DERIVED)

@context.$comment: imported through “The verified document returned from verification MUST be a well-formed compact JSON-LD document, as described in Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0080), which names the data model the verified document must conform to: “Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST include a @context property.” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.3). The returned document is the decoded payload (§5.1 to §5.3), so the payload carries it. Its value is not checked here.

type.$comment: imported through w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0080, as @context: “Verifiable credentials and verifiable presentations MUST contain a type property with an associated value.” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.5).

allOf.$comment: A presentation's verifiableCredential value, one object or an array of them, is enveloped: “Verifiable Credentials secured in verifiable presentations MUST use the Enveloped Verifiable Credential type defined by the [VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0021); w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0037; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0057. Absent is allowed (the source requires no credential in a presentation). An embedded credential with its own proof fails here, since these MUST statements name the Enveloped type.

“Verifiable Presentations in verifiable presentations MUST use the Enveloped Verifiable Presentation type defined by the [VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0022); w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0038; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0058. Where the payload is itself an EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation (Examples 3, 6, 9), it must be a well-formed one. Inferred scope: the source names no member that would carry a nested presentation anywhere else.

jwtClaimsSet.description: A JWT Claims Set that comprises a credential or presentation: the payload of vc+jwt or vp+jwt, and the claims an SD-JWT verifier rebuilds.

allOf.$comment: MUST NOT: “The JWT Claim Names vc and vp MUST NOT be present in any JWT Claims Set that comprises a verifiable credential or a verifiable presentation.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0006). Top-level members only: a JWT Claim Name is a member of the Claims Set object, so a property named vc inside credentialSubject is not one (inferred). §3.1.3, marked non-normative, restates the rule at line 369.

Registered claim value types, imported from RFC 7519 §4.1 through this source's §5.1, whose first step is “Follow the algorithm defined in Validating a JWT [RFC7519].” (§5.1): iss and sub StringOrURI, aud one string or an array of them, exp, nbf and iat NumericDate (a JSON number), jti a string. The source adds no constraint on these values; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0066 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0067 relate iss to issuer and are cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-01 and X-02. Claims this schema does not name are not restricted: “All claims that are not understood MUST be ignored.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0079).
